summary.text: 就 is commonly used for ‘go to,’ ‘approach,’ and ‘near.’ Its early forms are associated with a proposed scene of a temple above a raised platform, but the lower element and the relation between those early graphs and the later verb remain disputed.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. One analysis reads early forms as 亯 above 京, depicting a temple over a high platform and suggesting ritual at height. Later Qin and small-seal forms are reported as 京 + 尤, matching the Eastern Han dictionary’s analysis. Another account argues that some early forms had 止 below 京 and that later 又/尤 forms arose through graphic confusion. The evidence does not establish a single sequence or a secure phonetic role for 尤.

components.text: In the proposed early form, 亯 depicts a temple and supplies the setting for the suggested ritual-at-height scene. The reading of the early graphs as the later verb remains disputed.

京 is analyzed as a high platform or tower, supplying the raised setting in the proposed early scene. Its role there is pictorial; its appearance alongside 尤 in later analyses does not show that 尤 was present in the earliest form.

尤 appears in reported Qin and small-seal forms and in the Eastern Han dictionary’s analysis. Another account proposes 止 as an earlier lower element, with later 又/尤 forms arising through graphic confusion. 尤’s role in the graph remains disputed.

sound_limitation.text: The current Mandarin readings can be compared, but their resemblance does not establish a historical phonetic role. The cited Old Chinese forms are not a close match.

sound.text: In current Mandarin, 尤 yóu and 就 jiù share a glide and rhyme but differ in initial and tone. In the Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese system, their reconstructed forms, *[ɢ]ʷə and *[dz]u[k]-s, do not closely match.

history.text: Oracle-bone and bronze forms are analyzed as 亯 above 京; Chu forms are said to share strokes between these elements. Qin slips show 京 + 尤, a form reported as informing small-seal 就.

A competing analysis proposes an early lower 止 and suggests later 又/尤 forms reflect graphic confusion. The Eastern Han dictionary records 从京从尤 and a Zhou-script form 𡰜; this later account does not settle the earliest graph.

uncertainties.text: The early oracle-bone examples are mostly identified as place names. Their relation to the later verb, the lower element in the earliest forms, and the proposed ritual-at-height interpretation remain disputed.
Although 尤 occurs in some later analyses, its role as a phonetic element is not established; the early lower element is disputed, and the cited Old Chinese reconstructions do not closely match.

The phrase 申就乃命 is reported as a verbal use with a sense near ‘complete.’ Its connection to the early place-name use or the proposed ritual-at-height interpretation is not established.
In a Warring States route list, 就 is reported with the sense ‘go to.’ The evidence does not establish a continuous development from ‘high’ or ‘complete’ to this use.
‘Approach’ and ‘near’ are current glosses; their dates and development from earlier uses are not documented here.
‘Just’ and ‘simply’ are current glosses; their dates and development from earlier uses are not documented here.

limitations.text: The proposed ritual-at-height interpretation, early place-name examples, and later verbal uses are separate attestations; a semantic path connecting them is not established.

evidence.text: specialty
Phonosemantic compound. 京 represents the meaning and 尤 represents the sound. Based on the original meaning "achieve". The meaning of this character has shifted over time and now means "high place".
就，高也。从京从尤。尤，異於凡也。

Originally 𫢁, ideogrammic compound (會意 /会意): 享 + 京, a temple and a tower – meaning "to sacrifice at a high place". During the Warring States period, 享 was omitted. In seal script, 尤 (“especially; even more”) is added to the right, signifying "high; to go to a higher place".
Cognate with 造 (OC *skʰuːɡs, “to proceed to”) (Wang, 1982).
就，高也。从京从尤。尤，異於凡也。

evidence.field: 形義通解；就 的字形與早期用例
evidence.text: The database reports that oracle-bone and bronze forms of 就 are composed of 亯 and 京, interpreted as a temple form placed above a high platform, with the proposed sense ‘sacrifice at a high place.’ It says Chu forms share strokes between 亯 and 京, while the Qin slips first show the form 京 + 尤 that informed small-seal 就. It distinguishes early uses: oracle-bone examples are mostly place names; a Western Zhou inscriptional phrase 申就乃命 uses 就 verbally with a sense near ‘complete’; bronze examples also include travel uses, including 就郢 on the Warring States 鄂君啟車節. These are source analyses, not an uncontested chronology of all senses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：就

evidence.source: 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心；陳致
evidence.field: 金文、甲骨文與早期語義討論
evidence.text: The article reviews competing readings of early forms. It notes that most oracle-bone cases with the 亯 + 京 form are place names and are not attested as verbs in those contexts; it discusses the interpretation of an oracle-bone case as 就庸 as an earlier scholarly proposal. It identifies a mid-Western Zhou 史惠鼎 example in 日就月將, while discussing whether the phrase means continued increase/progress or has a ritual reading. Its author argues that the old graphic form included 亯 + high/京 + 止 and that later 又/尤 forms reflect graphic corruption of 止; the article also presents the alternative that Warring States 就 can be borrowed for 造 in travel contexts. This makes the identification of every early graph with the later verb and the explanation of the lower component disputed.
evidence.kind: scholarly paleographic argument with explicit competing analyses
evidence.title: 陳致：“日居月諸”與“日就月將”：早期四言詩與祭祀禮辭釋例

evidence.text: Xu Shen’s Eastern Han dictionary defines 就 as ‘high’ and analyzes it as 从京从尤, explaining 尤 as ‘different from the ordinary’; it also records 𡰜 as a Zhou-script form. This is an important historical account but does not by itself establish that the earliest graphic form had 尤 or that 尤 was originally the phonetic element.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：就（《說文》引文）

evidence.text: The database analyzes archaic 京 as depicting a tall platform or tower, with its original sense ‘large/high platform’; it reports later uses for place names and the capital, and cites the Shuowen definition ‘a very high mound made by people.’ 京 is thus an independently semantic element in the earliest proposed 就 graphic analysis, not evidence for the later component’s sound role.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：京

evidence.text: The database reports a bronze form of 尤 as 又 plus a small extra mark, interpreted by cited scholars as a hand bearing a growth; it gives the proposed original sense ‘wart/lump’ and extensions including ‘unusual’ and ‘especially.’ It also reproduces the Shuowen analysis of 尤 as ‘different’ and 又 as phonetic. These descriptions make semantic motivation for the Shuowen explanation intelligible, but they do not establish that 尤 was the lower component in the earliest 就 graph.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：尤

evidence.text: In the Baxter–Sagart 2014 notation, 尤 yóu is MC hjuw and OC *[ɢ]ʷə; 就 jiù is MC dzjuwH and OC *[dz]u[k]-s, glossed ‘go to.’ These entries do not furnish a close direct Old Chinese rhyme match that would independently demonstrate 尤 as the phonetic in 就. Their MC forms are source-data notation, not reconstructions.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The precise identification and semantic value of the earliest oracle-bone 亯 + 京 examples remain disputed: available sources report them mostly as place names and record an older proposed verb interpretation, but do not settle whether they represent 就 in the later verbal sense.

A direct semantic development from ‘high’/‘sacrifice on a high place’ to verbal senses such as ‘complete’ or ‘go to/approach’ is not established by the inspected evidence. The early attested uses are distinct and should not be arranged as a simple dictionary-gloss chronology.

The lower element in the earliest graphic is unsettled: sources variously describe 尤 in the Qin/small-seal form, a prior 止 element with later graphic confusion, and an early pictographic/semantic 亯 + 京 formation. Consequently, a secure phonetic role for 尤 in the earliest 就 is not established. Baxter–Sagart entries give 尤 *[ɢ]ʷə versus 就 *[dz]u[k]-s; local rows for 京 and 就 preserve their exact notation, and do not establish 尤 as a matching phonetic.

The role of 京 in the later formation is reported as semantic in Shuowen, but the early 亯 + 京 graph analysis assigns 京 a graphic/semantic role in the ‘high platform’ scene rather than identifying the whole graph as an ordinary phono-semantic compound.

Official Unicode Unihan character-specific URLs for U+4EAC, U+5C31 and U+5C24 were attempted but inaccessible to the web tool. Local exact reading rows were checked, and accessible nonofficial mirror pages were inspected; the requested official per-character click-through verification remains a limitation.
No glyph images were visually inspected; graphic descriptions above are source-reported analyses.

The early oracle-bone graphs are mostly reported as place names; whether they are the same lexeme as later verbal 就 is not established. The cited proposed interpretation 就庸 is a minority/older reading.

The relationship from proposed ‘ritual at height’ or ‘high’ to later ‘complete’ and ‘go to/approach’ is not demonstrated as a continuous semantic chronology. The cited uses should remain separate attestations rather than ordered glosses.

The earliest lower element is disputed: Fudan argues some early forms included 止 and that later 又/尤 forms may be graphic corruption; CUHK describes Qin slips with 京 + 尤. The Shuowen component analysis is historical testimony, not confirmation of the earliest structure.

The role of 尤 as phonetic in the later graph is not securely established by these sources. Baxter–Sagart gives 尤 *[ɢ]ʷə and 就 *[dz]u[k]-s; the sound comparison does not support a simple close match. No independently established pronunciation of a depicted object is relevant here because no whole-graph loan claim is adopted.

The local Baxter–Sagart and Unihan row metadata supplied in the dossier was not independently re-read from repository files in this invocation. Official Unicode U+4EAC, U+5C31 and U+5C24 pages were attempted and inaccessible; CUHK entries supplied current reading metadata but are not official Unihan records.

No glyph image was visually inspected. The CUHK image links identify candidate script-form examples but the database's reuse terms for those specific image assets were not verified, so no image is proposed. Xiaoxuetang's applicable CC0 notice was verified, but its exact 就 query/image could not be retrieved.

limitations.text: The proposed early forms of 就 remain disputed: the oracle-bone graphs are mostly identified as place names, and scholars disagree about the lower element and whether those graphs represent the later verb. The proposed ritual-at-height interpretation is not established as a continuous origin for later senses.
